captions.caption: The dwarf irregular galaxy NGC 5264 is located 15 million light years away. It is only about 11,000 light years across, much smaller than our Milky Way, and consists of approximately a billion stars. It lacks the spiral structure of our home Galaxy. The small blue patches in NGC 5264 mark groups of young hot blue stars. This suggests that stars formation in this galaxy is still on-going.
captions.alt_text: NGC 5264 appears as a light, fuzzy, ragged oval on a dark background. Some single stars are visible amongst its diffuse glow
